children: Lean hog futures extend losses to three sessions amid a decline in cutout prices, with all cuts lower except ham. "Pork prices are cheap especially compared to beef, but not chicken," Chris Lehner of ADM Investor Services says in a note. Since pork associations pushed it as the "other white meat," many consumers now see it as that, plus they aren't cooking large cuts like loin and hams. "Consumers want fast-cooking meats," he adds. Most-active hogs fall 2.2% to 69.65 cents a pound. Live cattle slip 0.8% to $2.2335 a pound.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
